name: stri_count_charclass
title: Count the Number of Pattern Occurrences

origin.description: Count how many code points in each string belong to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: Character vector of strings to search.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error.

origin.details: The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Each match is one code point. A missing string or pattern yields NA. An empty string with a real pattern counts as 0. \p{Z} is the separator category. \p{WhiteSpace} also includes tab and newline. U+200B is in neither.
origin.value: An integer vector. A missing result is NA.
origin.example:
x <- stri_count_charclass("stringi", "\\p{L}")
sentence <- paste0('stri_count_charclass("stringi", "\\p{L}") returns ', x, '.')
writeLines(sentence)

translation.description: Count how many code points in each string belong to a character class.

arguments.name: str
arguments.text: String, missing value, or list of those.

arguments.name: pattern
arguments.text: An ICU UnicodeSet pattern: \p{L}, \p{N}, \p{WhiteSpace}, [:WhiteSpace:], or [a-z]. A bare name such as WhiteSpace, and \w, are not patterns. An empty pattern is an error. Membership is ICU 76, Unicode 16.

translation.details: The inputs are recycled to the longer length. Each match is one code point. A missing string or pattern yields NA. An empty string with a real pattern counts as 0. The class is built with icu.UnicodeSet. U+105C0 is a letter in ICU 76 and unassigned in Python unicodedata 15.1.
translation.value: A list of integers. A missing result is NA. None as str is an empty list.
translation.example:
from stringi.charclass import stri_count_charclass
x = stri_count_charclass("stringi", "\\p{L}")
sentence = f'stri_count_charclass("stringi", "\\p{{L}}") returns {x[0]}.'
print(sentence)
